text:
Morgan: FYI PlaylistPro is hitting 429s in prod EU starting ~09:05 UTC, customer says it started after they rolled out a scheduled sync job.
Sasha: Can you paste the 429 response headers we saw in the gateway logs? especially Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* if present.
Morgan: got it, log snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 09:05:12 GMT
Retry-After: 60
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Content-Type: application/json
```
PlaylistPro Ops: our team pushed a large refetch across tenants at 09:05 to fix a data drift bug — it was ~12k requests across 8 tokens, aligned to a cron at minute boundary.
Carlos: that looks like RPM alignment. Are they using a single API token per tenant or pooling? if single token per tenant, top-of-minute bursts will blow past bucket.
Mei: asking for their SDK version and concurrency pattern. also would like example of request rate per token per 60s window.
PlaylistPro Ops: SDK v2.3.1, we use per-tenant tokens and spawn 50 worker goroutines that execute the sync for each tenant at the same minute. we didn't add jitter.
Sasha: immediate mitigation options (quick list):
- add jitter to cron window (+/- 30s)
- reduce parallelism per token (workers-> 5)
- implement token pooling across tenants so requests spread
- honor Retry-After and implement exponential backoff with jitter
I can push a short patch to their orchestration if they want.
PlaylistPro Ops: can we get a temporary quota bump while we patch? this affects paying customers.
Morgan: I created a support ticket and looped infra. Ticket #SUP-8427. Requested emergency uplift for EU region for 2 hours.
InfraBot: Emergency quota change request received: SUP-8427. Please include traffic dump (headers + timestamps) for audit.
Carlos: quick repro script I asked them to run to validate fix (runs at 1 request every 200ms by default):
```
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..300}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.2
done
```
Mei: also asked them to run same script but randomized start time across 60s to simulate jitter and compare 429s.
PlaylistPro Ops: ran. aligned-run -> 38% 429s; jittered-run -> 2% 429s. patch works.
Sasha: infra findings: per-tenant RPM in EU is 600/min default. We observed >900 requests/min for several tokens at 09:05 -> automatic 429. Gateway shows minute-rolled buckets caused the spike to be concentrated; adding jitter spreads over windows.
InfraBot: No server-side bug found; behavior consistent with rate-limiter policy. Audit trail attached to SUP-8427.
Carlos: recommended long-term: implement client-side request pacing and token pooling. also consider per-tenant rate limits if a single tenant owns many tokens.
Mei: documented a short playbook -> asked to add to internal runbook: "cron jobs: always jitter + cap worker concurrency; verify with staging replay". I'll add step-by-step.
PlaylistPro Ops: we applied concurrency cap and jitter. our customers are green. thanks.
Morgan: closing loop: infra gave a 1-hour emergency uplift while patch deployed, then revoked. Ticket updated with repro and mitigation steps.
Sasha: dropping a sample backoff snippet we recommended to them (golang):
```
for attempt := 0; attempt < 5; attempt++ {
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if resp != nil && resp.StatusCode == 429 {
    ra := resp.Header.Get("Retry-After")
    wait, _ := strconv.Atoi(ra)
    time.Sleep(time.Duration(wait)*time.Second + time.Duration(rand.Intn(500))*time.Millisecond)
    continue
  }
  // handle success
}
```
Carlos: note: if upstream traffic pattern is a cron fanout across many tokens, even short burst can exhaust cluster-level concurrent slots. we suggested they also ramp gradually when doing mass fixes.
Mei: I'll add the incident summary to support folder and tag with SUP-8427 and playlistpro.
Morgan: thanks everyone. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
